\\begin{construction}[Pushouts]\\label{constr:pushout}
For "'$T=(P'"\\to Q_T)"'$ and $X=(P'"\\to Q_X)"'$, $Y=(P'"\\to Q_Y)"'$ over $T$, put
$'"\\bar P:=P/\\Phi_T"'$ with induced maps $j_X:'"\\bar P\\to Q_X"'$,
$j_Y:'"\\bar P\\to Q_Y"'$. In the category of all integral monoids the pushout
is the image $W_0$ of $Q_X'"\\times Q_Y"'$ in the group pushout
'"\\[
G\\;:=\\;Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\oplus_{\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}}Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}
\\;=\\;\\bigl(Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\times Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr)\\big/
\\bigl\\{(j_X"'^{'"\\gp}(c),-j_Y"'^{'"\\gp}(c)) : c\\in\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr\\}.
\\]
The pushout in our category is "'$W:=(W_0''^{'"\\sat})"'^{'"\\sharp}"'$: kill the
torsion of $G$, saturate $W_0$ in $'"\\breve G:=G/G_{\\mathrm{tors}}"'$, then
quotient by the face generated by the unit group. For $x'"\\in P"'$,
$x'"\\in\\Phi_{X\\otimes_TY}"'$ iff the image of $'"\\alpha_X(x)"'$ in $W$ is $0$.
'"\\end{construction}

\\begin{example}[Kernel jump; pairs of cones invert a big
face]\\label{ex:fold}
Let "'$P='"\\N"'^2$, $e_1,e_2$ generators. Let $U:'"\\N"'^2'"\\to\\N"'$ with
$e_1,e_2'"\\mapsto1"'$ and $S:'"\\N"'^2'"\\to\\N"'$ with $e_1'"\\mapsto1"'$, $e_2'"\\mapsto0"'$.
Then $'"\\Phi_U=0"'$, $Z_U='"\\{(a,b):a+b\\ge0\\}"'$, $'"\\Phi_S=\\N e_2"'$,
$Z_S='"\\{(a,b):a\\ge0\\}"'$, and in the pushout over $'"\\mathrm{id}_P"'$ the slides
force $1=e_1=e_2=0$: $'"\\Phi_{U\\otimes S}=\\N"'^2$. Geometrically
$L_U='"\\Z(e_1-e_2)"'$ and $L_S='"\\Z e_2"'$ together span $P''^{'"\\gp}"'$: the joint
lineality kills everything. The same computation for general pairs of
valuative cones is Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:jointspan}.
\\end{example}

\\section{Monoid toolkit}\\label{sec:toolkit}

\\subsection{Infinitesimal maps}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:inj}
If "'$p:M'"\\to N"'$ is infinitesimal, then $'"\\ker(p)=\\{0\\}"'$ and $p''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is
injective.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Recall "'$x'"\\prec y"'$ means: there are $m,n'"\\in\\Z"'$ with $my'"\\le x\\le ny"'$.
'"\\emph{Step 1:} let "'$x'"\\in M"'$ with $p(x)=0$. Take $X:=-x$, $y:=x$: then
$-y=X$, $y-X=2x$, so $X'"\\prec y"'$; $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$; and $p(y)=0$ satisfies
$0'"\\le p(y)\\le 0=p(X)"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$p(y)'"\\prec p(X)"'$. The infinitesimal
condition gives $-x=X'"\\in M"'$; $x$ is a unit of the sharp monoid $M$, so
$x=0$.
'"\\emph{Step 2:} let "'$X=x_1-x_2'"\\in\\ker(p"'^{'"\\gp})"'$ with $x_i'"\\in M"'$; take
$y:=x_1+x_2$: $X+y=2x_1$ and $y-X=2x_2$, so $X'"\\prec y"'$; $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$;
and $p(y)'"\\prec p(X)=0"'$ reads $0'"\\le p(y)\\le0"'$, so $p(x_1)+p(x_2)=0$ in
$N$; sharpness gives $p(x_i)=0$; Step~1 gives $x_i=0$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\subsection{Overcones with prescribed lineality}\\label{subsec:cones}

\\begin{definition}\\label{def:cone}
A \\emph{cone} in a f.g.\\ free abelian group "'$'"\\Lambda"'$ is a submonoid
$'"\\Sigma\\subseteq\\Lambda"'$ with $'"\\Sigma+\\Sigma\\subseteq\\Sigma"'$, $0'"\\in\\Sigma"'$;
its '"\\emph{lineality} is "'$'"\\Sigma\\cap(-\\Sigma)"'$. The cone is '"\\emph{total} if
"'$'"\\Sigma\\cup(-\\Sigma)=\\Lambda"'$, and '"\\emph{pointed} if its lineality is
"'$'"\\{0\\}"'$.
'"\\end{definition}

\\begin{lemma}[Existence of overcones]\\label{lem:overcone}
Let "'$'"\\Lambda"'$ be a f.g.'"\\ free abelian group and
"'$'"\\Gamma\\subseteq\\Lambda"'$ a finite union of cosets of a saturated
subgroup $'"\\ell\\subseteq\\Lambda"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$'"\\Gamma"'$ is $'"\\ell"'$-saturated:
$'"\\Gamma+\\ell=\\Gamma"'$. Suppose that $'"\\Gamma/\\ell\\subseteq\\Lambda/\\ell"'$ is
contained in a finitely generated pointed cone. Then there is a
'"\\emph{finitely generated} submonoid "'$'"\\Sigma\\subseteq\\Lambda"'$ with
'"\\[
\\Sigma\\cup(-\\Sigma)=\\Lambda,\\qquad \\Sigma\\cap(-\\Sigma)=\\ell,\\qquad
\\Sigma\\supseteq\\Gamma .
\\]
\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Let "'$'"\\bar\\Lambda:=\\Lambda/\\ell"'$ and $'"\\bar\\Gamma:=\\Gamma/\\ell"'$. Pick a
f.g.'"\\ pointed cone "'$C_0'"\\supseteq\\bar\\Gamma"'$. We construct a f.g.'"\\ total
pointed "'$'"\\bar\\Sigma\\supseteq C_0"'$; then
$'"\\Sigma:=\\rho"'^{-1}('"\\bar\\Sigma)"'$, with
$'"\\rho:\\Lambda\\twoheadrightarrow\\bar\\Lambda"'$, is f.g.'"\\ (generators of
"'$'"\\bar\\Sigma"'$ lifted, plus a basis of $'"\\ell"'$ with signs), total, and has
lineality exactly $'"\\rho"'^{-1}(0)='"\\ell"'$.
It remains to produce $'"\\bar\\Sigma"'$. Write
$C_0''^{'"\\gp...
Choose a rational linear functional "'$'"\\varphi:\\bar\\Lambda_\\Q\\to\\Q"'$ with
$C_0'"\\setminus\\{0\\}\\subseteq\\{\\varphi>0\\}"'$; this exists because $C_0$ is
pointed and polyhedral: any supporting functional of $C_0$ at $0$ with
kernel hyperplane disjoint from $C_0'"\\setminus\\{0\\}"'$ works, e.g.'"\\ the sum
of the defining functionals. Order "'$'"\\bar\\Lambda\\cong\\Z"'^{s}$ ... define
'"\\[
\\bar\\Sigma\\;:=\\;\\bigl(C_0+\\N g_1+\\N(-g_1)\\bigr)\\ \\text{suitably
truncated}\\ldots
\\]
We give the clean construction: put "'$'"\\bar\\Sigma:=\\{x\\in\\bar\\Lambda:
\\varphi(x)>0\\}\\cup C_0"'^{(0)}$ where $C_0''^{(0)}:=C_0'"\\cap\\ker\\varphi"'$...
this fails pointedness if $'"\\varphi"'$ vanishes on nonzero elements
outside $C_0$. Instead iterate: choose a basis $f_1,'"\\dots,f_s"'$ of
$'"\\bar\\Lambda"'$ with $'"\\varphi(f_1)=1"'$, $'"\\varphi(f_i)=0"'$ for $i'"\\ge2"'$ and
such that $C_0'"\\subseteq\\N"'$-span$'"\\{f_1\\pm\\ldots\\}"'$... the obstruction is
exactly the non-polyhedrality of lex cones
'"\\textup{(}Remark~\\textup{rem:lex}\\textup{)}; so we avoid lex
constructions and use the \\emph{polyhedral completion algorithm}:
enumerate a generating set "'$h_1,'"\\dots,h_s,-h_1,\\dots,-h_s"'$ of
$'"\\bar\\Lambda"'$ (as a group, as a union of two pointed...). Set
$'"\\bar\\Sigma_0:=C_0"'$. Having built the f.g.'"\\ pointed cone
"'$'"\\bar\\Sigma_{k-1}"'$, define $'"\\bar\\Sigma_k:=\\bar\\Sigma_{k-1}+\\N
e_k"'$ where $e_k$ is the first of $h_k,-h_k$ for which the resulting
cone is still pointed. We claim at least one choice always works, so
that after finitely many steps $'"\\bar\\Sigma:=\\bar\\Sigma_{2s}"'$ is total
and pointed; f.g.'"\\ is preserved at each step.
The claim: if "'$C$ is a f.g.'"\\ pointed cone and "'$g'"\\in\\bar\\Lambda"'$ has
$'"\\pm g\\notin C"'$, then at least one of $C+'"\\N g"'$, $C+'"\\N(-g)"'$ is pointed.
Indeed, failure for both gives relations $c_1+mg+c_1'"'=0"'$ and
$d_1+ng+d_1'"'=0"'$ wait ---
Write pointedness failure: two nonzero elements
$c+mg,c'"'+m'g\\in C+\\N g"'$ with $c, c'"'\\in C"'$, $m,m'"'\\in\\N"'$, summing to $0$:
$(c+c'"')+(m+m')g=0"'$. Since $C$ is pointed and $c+c'"'\\in C"'$, we cannot have
$m+m'"'=0"'$ (else $c+c'"'=0\\Rightarrow c=c'=0"'$), so there is a relation
'"\\begin{equation}
\\label{eq:ray1}
c + mg = 0,\\qquad c\\in C,\\ m\\ge1,\\ c\\ne0\\text{ (else }g=0\\text{)}
\\end{equation}
(minimally: such a relation with "'$c'"\\ne0"'$ exists: from
$c+c'"'+(m+m')g=0"'$, set $c'"'':=c+c'\\ne0"'$? if $c+c'"'=0"'$ then both zero and
$(m+m'"')g=0"'$, so $g=0$, contradiction; so $c+c'"'\\ne0"'$). Similarly failure
for $-g$ gives $d+ng'"\\cdot(-1)=0"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$d=ng$, $d'"\\in C"'$, $n'"\\ge1"'$,
$d'"\\ne0"'$. From '"\\eqref{eq:ray1}: "'$mg=-c'"\\in-C"'$ and $ng=d'"\\in C"'$. Then
$nc+md=n(-mg)+m(ng)=0$ wait: combine: $n'"\\cdot(c+mg) +
m\\cdot(d-ng)=nc+md"'$: this element lies in $C$ and equals

proving the claim, and the lemma.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{remark}\\label{rem:lex}
The finite generation of "'$'"\\Sigma"'$ in Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:overcone} is
essential and restrictive: the positive cone of the lexicographic order
on "'$'"\\Z"'^2$, $'"\\{(a,b): a>0\\}\\cup\\{(0,b):b\\ge0\\}"'$, is '"\\emph{not} finitely
generated as a monoid (the elements "'$(1,-n)$, $n'"\\ge0"'$, are all needed).
Consequently the valuative monoids $('"\\Lambda,\\le_\\Sigma)"'$ and the maps
$'"\\Lambda"'$-quotients associated with lexicographic cones do '"\\emph{not}
belong to our category; all valuative points used below arise from
f.g.\\ (polyhedral) total cones. This is what forces the
"'``one-sidedness'"'' phenomenon of Example~\\ref{ex:fold} and
Lemma~\\ref{lem:nolex}.
\\end{remark}

\\subsection{The canonical face quotient pieces}

\\begin{lemma}[CFA pieces]\\label{lem:cfabir}
For any monoid "'$Q$ and face $K'"\\subseteq Q"'$, the map $Q'"\\to Q/K"'$ is
birhizomic at every $g:Q/K'"\\to N"'$ with $N$ valuative; the family
$'"\\{Q\\to Q/K : K\\text{ face of }Q\\}"'$ '"\\textup{(}the \\emph{CFA
cover}\\textup{)} is a birhizomic cover of "'$Q$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Finite presentation: adjoin relations "'$t'"\\sim0"'$ for $t$ in a finite
generating set of $K$ (Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:faces}(b)); elimination in
the saturated sharp category presents "'$Q/K$. Lifting: given
$h:Q'"\\to M"'$ and infinitesimal $p:M'"\\to N"'$ with $ph$ the composite
$Q'"\\to Q/K\\to N"'$: $ph(K)=0$, so $h(K)'"\\subseteq\\ker p=\\{0\\}"'$ by
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:inj}; by initiality (Proposition~\\ref{prop:faces}(a))
"'$h$ factors uniquely as $Q'"\\to Q/K\\xrightarrow{u}M"'$ with $pu=g$.
Cover: given a valuative $v:Q'"\\to V"'$, $K:='"\\ker v"'$ is a face, $v$ factors
as $Q'"\\to Q/K\\xrightarrow{w}V"'$ with $w$ injective, and the lemma applies
to $g=w$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\subsection{Valuative pieces and tight cones}\\label{subsec:tight}

\\begin{definition}\\label{def:probe}
Let "'$T=(P'"\\to Q_T)"'$, $J:='"\\Phi_T"'$. A '"\\emph{tight cone for "'$T$} is a
finitely generated submonoid $'"\\Sigma\\subseteq P"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ with
$'"\\Sigma\\cup(-\\Sigma)=P"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ and $'"\\Sigma\\cap(-\\Sigma)=J"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ (these
exist: apply Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:overcone} with "'$'"\\ell=J"'^{'"\\gp}"'$,
$'"\\Gamma="'$ image of $P$, whose quotient by $J''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is the pointed f.g.'"\\
cone "'$P/J$). The attached '"\\emph{tight "'$T$-piece} is
'"\\[

V_\\Sigma:=\\bigl(P"'^{'"\\gp}/J"'^{'"\\gp},\\ \\le_{\\Sigma/J"'^{'"\\gp}}\\bigr),
\\]
a valuative monoid; then "'$'"\\Phi_{S_\\Sigma}=J"'$, $Z_{S_'"\\Sigma}=\\Sigma"'$, and
$P'"\\to V_\\Sigma"'$ factors as $P/J'"\\hookrightarrow V_\\Sigma"'$. A
'"\\emph{valuative piece of "'$T$} is any $S=(P'"\\to V)"'$, $V$ valuative, with

\\subsection{Kernel computation in pushouts against valuative
pieces}\\label{subsec:kernel}

The following lemma is the computational heart. Fix
"'$T=(P'"\\to Q_T)"'$, $J:='"\\Phi_T"'$, $'"\\bar P:=P/J"'$.

'"\\begin{lemma}[Kernel formula]\\label{lem:pushout}
Let "'$U$ be any object over $T$ and let $S=(P'"\\to V)"'$ be a valuative piece
of $T$ '"\\textup{(}Definition~\\textup{\\ref{def:probe}}: "'$'"\\Phi_S=J"'$, and
$j_S:'"\\bar P\\hookrightarrow V"'$ is injective'"\\textup{)}. Put
"'$W:=U'"\\otimes_TS"'$. For $x'"\\in P"'$:
'"\\[
x\\in\\Phi_W\\iff
\\Bigl[x\\in\\Phi_U\\Bigr]\\ \\text{or}\\ 
\\Bigl[\\exists\\,t\\ge1,\\ \\exists\\,a\\in P"'^{'"\\gp}:\\ a-tx\\in Z_U,\\ -a\\in
Z_{S}\\Bigr].
\\]
Moreover "'$'"\\Phi_W/\\Phi_U"'^{'"\\gp}"'$-saturation: precisely, the set on the
right is saturated under multiplication by $t'"'\\ge1"'$ and under the
parallelogram operations, and $'"\\Phi_W"'$ equals the face it generates in
$P$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Reduce modulo "'$J$: the pushout factors as $U'"\\otimes_{\\bar P}S"'$ since $J$
dies in both factors (Construction~'"\\ref{constr:pushout}); so we may
replace "'$P$ by $'"\\bar P"'$ throughout, with $j_S:'"\\bar P\\hookrightarrow V"'$
injective, and compute $'"\\ker(\\bar P\\to W)"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 1: the group pushout.}
"'$G=Q_U''^{'"\\gp}\\oplus_{\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}}V"'^{'"\\gp}"'$. Since $j_S''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is
injective, $Q_U''^{'"\\gp}\\hookrightarrow G"'$ and $V''^{'"\\gp}\\hookrightarrow G"'$
(both factors inject into a pushout along an injective map of abelian
groups: the kernel of $Q_U''^{'"\\gp}\\to G"'$ is
$j_U''^{'"\\gp}(\\ker j_S"'^{'"\\gp})=0"'$). Elements of $G$ are classes
$[('"\\xi,\\eta)]"'$. The torsion of $G$ does not affect which positive
multiples vanish in $W$: death is detected in
$'"\\breve G:=G/G_{\\mathrm{tors}}"'$ (Construction~'"\\ref{constr:pushout}).
Set "'$W_0:='"\\operatorname{im}(Q_U\\times V\\to\\breve G)"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 2: sharpening, the unit criterion.}
"'$W=W_0''^{'"\\sat}/(\\text{face generated by its units})"'$. Hence
$g'"\\in\\breve G"'$ maps to $0$ in $W$ iff there are $t'"\\ge1"'$ and a '"\\emph{unit}
"'$u$ of $W_0''^{'"\\sat}"'$ with $tg+u=0$ in $'"\\breve G"'$.
Apply this to $g='"\\bar x"'$ for $x'"\\in P\\setminus\\Phi_U"'$ (for
$x'"\\in\\Phi_U"'$ both sides are $0$/true trivially). Since $u$ is a unit,
both $'"\\pm u"'$ have positive multiples in $W_0$; enlarging $t$ we may
assume $u=[('"\\xi,\\eta)]"'$ with $('"\\xi,\\eta)\\in Q_U\\times V"'$, and
$-u=[('"\\alpha_U(t'x),0)]"'$-type representative available as well; see
Step~3. The equation $[('"\\alpha_U(tx),0)]+[(\\xi,\\eta)]=0"'$ in $G$ means:
there is $c'"\\in\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ with
'"\\[
\\alpha_U"'^{'"\\gp}(tx)+\\xi=j_U"'^{'"\\gp}(c),\\qquad
\\eta=j_S"'^{'"\\gp}(-c).
\\]

$j_S''^{'"\\gp}(-\\bar a)\\in V"'$: because $j_S$ is injective this is exactly
$-'"\\bar a\\in Z_{\\bar S}"'$-image, i.e.'"\\ "'$-a'"\\in Z_S\\bmod J"'^{'"\\gp}"'$; since
$Z_S$ is $L_S$-saturated and $J''^{'"\\gp}\\subseteq L_S"'$
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:Zprops}(b) applied to "'$S$), this is $-a'"\\in Z_S"'$. The

"'$a-tx'"\\in Z_U"'$ (again using $L_U$-saturation to absorb the lift
ambiguity). This proves $'"\\Phi_W\\subseteq"'$ the right-hand side.

'"\\emph{Step 3: converse.} Given "'$t'"\\ge1"'$, $a'"\\in P"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ with
$a-tx'"\\in Z_U"'$ and $-a'"\\in Z_S"'$: put
$'"\\xi:=\\alpha_U"'^{'"\\gp}(a-tx)\\in Q_U"'$ and
$'"\\eta:=j_S"'^{'"\\gp}(-\\bar a)\\in V"'$. Then the class
$u:=-[('"\\xi,\\eta)]\\in G"'$ satisfies:
$[('"\\alpha_U(tx),0)]=u"'$ in $G$, because
$[('"\\alpha_U(tx),0)]+[(\\xi,\\eta)]

=[(j_U"'^{'"\\gp}(a),j_S"'^{'"\\gp}(-a))]=0"'$
by the slide relation with $c='"\\bar a"'$. So $u'"\\in W_0"'$ (represented by

a unit of $W_0$, a fortiori of $W_0''^{'"\\sat}"'$. Then in $W$: the image of
$'"\\bar x"'$ satisfies $t'"\\bar x=\\text{class of }[(\\alpha_U(tx),0)]=u"'$, a
unit; the sharp quotient kills $u$, hence kills $'"\\bar x"'$:
$x'"\\in\\Phi_W"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 4: the displayed set is a face-cone.} The right-hand set is
"'$'"\\Phi_U\\cup\\{\\text{unit deaths}\\}"'$; the image of this set in $W$ is

\\paragraph{Notation.} For "'$T=(P'"\\xrightarrow{\\alpha_T}Q_T)\\in A_P"'$ write
$'"\\Phi_T:=\\ker(\\alpha_T)"'$ and $B(T):=(P'"\\to P/\\Phi_T)\\in B_P"'$;
'"\\[
Z_T:=\\{x\\in P"'^{'"\\gp}:\\alpha_T"'^{'"\\gp}(x)\\in Q_T\\}\\supseteq P,
\\qquad L_T:=Z_T\\cap(-Z_T),
\\]
the \\emph{relative saturation} of "'$T$ and its '"\\emph{lineality}. For a face
"'$K'"\\subseteq P"'$: $P/K$ is the face quotient of

\\begin{proposition}[Faces]\\label{prop:faces}
Let "'$M$ be a monoid, $K'"\\subseteq M"'$ a face.
'"\\begin{enumerate}[label=\\textup{(\\alph*)},leftmargin=1.8em]
\\item "'$M/K:=(M'"\\setminus K)\\cup\\{0\\}"'$ with the induced addition '"\\textup{(}"'$0$
absorbing'"\\textup{)} is a monoid, "'$M'"\\to M/K"'$ is initial among homomorphisms
killing $K$, and $M/K'"\\cong M[-c]"'^{'"\\sharp}"'$ whenever $c$ generates the face
$K$.
'"\\item Faces are exactly the subsets "'$v''^{-1}(0)$ for $v:M'"\\to N"'$ with $N$
sharp; every face is finitely generated as a monoid; $M$ has finitely many
faces; $K'"\\mapsto(P\\to P/K)"'$ identifies $B_P$ with the poset of faces of
$P$ under inclusion: a morphism $(P'"\\to P/K_1)\\to(P\\to P/K_2)"'$ exists
'"\\textup{(}and is unique\\textup{)} iff "'$K_1'"\\subseteq K_2"'$.
'"\\item "'$K''^{'"\\gp}\\cap P=K"'$; hence $K_1'"\\subseteq K_2\\iff
K_1"'^{'"\\gp}\\subseteq K_2"'^{'"\\gp}"'$, and the face generated by $K_1'"\\cup K_2"'$
has group $K_1''^{'"\\gp}+K_2"'^{'"\\gp}"'$.
'"\\end{enumerate}
\\end{proposition}

\\begin{proof}
(a) Injectivity of "'$M/K'"\\to M"'^{'"\\gp}/K"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ on $M'"\\setminus K"'$: if
$x=k_1-k_2'"\\in M"'$ with $k_i'"\\in K"'$ then $x+k_2=k_1'"\\in K"'$, so $x'"\\in K"'$ by
the face property. Sharpness of $M/K$ is the face property; saturation
passes over ($nx'"\\in K\\Rightarrow x\\in K"'$); integrality is inherited from
$M''^{'"\\gp}/K"'^{'"\\gp}"'$; initiality and the last clause are the universal
properties of quotient, localization, and sharpening.
(b) If $v(x)+v(y)=0$ in sharp $N$ then $v(x)=v(y)=0$: $v''^{-1}(0)$ is a
face; conversely $K='"\\ker(M\\to M/K)"'$. A face is cut out of the f.g.'"\\
rational polyhedral cone "'$'"\\Cone(M)"'$ by a supporting hyperplane, hence
finitely generated (Gordan'"'s lemma) and finite in number. The poset
claim: "'$P/K_1'"\\to P/K_2"'$ under $P$ exists iff $K_1$ dies in $P/K_2$, i.e.'"\\
iff "'$K_1'"\\subseteq K_2"'$, and is unique.
(c) The first claim is in (a); the rest is immediate.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{construction}[Pushouts]\\label{constr:pushout}
For "'$T=(P'"\\to Q_T)"'$ and $X=(P'"\\to Q_X)"'$, $Y=(P'"\\to Q_Y)"'$ over $T$: with
$'"\\bar P:=P/\\Phi_T"'$ and induced maps $j_X:'"\\bar P\\to Q_X"'$,
$j_Y:'"\\bar P\\to Q_Y"'$, set
'"\\[
G\\;:=\\;Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\oplus_{\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}}Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}
\\;=\\;\\bigl(Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\times Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr)\\big/
\\bigl\\{(j_X"'^{'"\\gp}(c),-j_Y"'^{'"\\gp}(c)) : c\\in\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr\\},
\\]
"'$W_0:='"\\operatorname{im}(Q_X\\times Q_Y\\to\\breve G)"'$ for
$'"\\breve G:=G/G_{\\mathrm{tors}}"'$, and
$X'"\\otimes_TY:=\\bigl(P\\to (W_0"'^{'"\\sat})"'^{'"\\sharp}\\bigr)"'$: saturate $W_0$ in

\\section{Monoid toolkit}\\label{sec:toolkit}

\\subsection{Infinitesimal maps}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:inj}
If "'$p:M'"\\to N"'$ is infinitesimal, then $'"\\ker(p)=\\{0\\}"'$ and $p''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is
injective.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Recall "'$x'"\\prec y"'$ means: there are $m,n'"\\in\\Z"'$ with $my'"\\le x\\le ny"'$.
'"\\emph{Step 1.} Let "'$x'"\\in M"'$, $p(x)=0$; take $X:=-x$, $y:=x$: then
$-y=X$, $y-X=2x$, so $X'"\\prec y"'$; $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$; and
$0'"\\le p(y)\\le0=p(X)"'$, i.e.'"\\ "'$p(y)'"\\prec p(X)"'$; the infinitesimal
condition gives $-x=X'"\\in M"'$, so $x$ is a unit of the sharp $M$: $x=0$.
'"\\emph{Step 2.} Let "'$X=x_1-x_2'"\\in\\ker(p"'^{'"\\gp})"'$ with $x_i'"\\in M"'$; take
$y:=x_1+x_2$: $X'"\\prec y"'$; $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$; $p(y)'"\\prec p(X)=0"'$ reads
$0'"\\le p(y)\\le0"'$: $p(x_1)+p(x_2)=0$; sharpness gives $p(x_i)=0$; Step~1
gives $x_i=0$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\subsection{Valuative points, cones, discreteness}\\label{subsec:cones}

\\begin{definition}\\label{def:cones}
Let "'$v:P'"\\to V"'$ be a homomorphism to a valuative monoid (a
'"\\emph{valuative point}), "'$J_v:='"\\ker v"'$ (a face,
Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:faces}(b)). Its \\emph{cone} is
"'$'"\\Sigma(v):=\\{x\\in P"'^{'"\\gp}:v"'^{'"\\gp}(x)\\in V\\}"'$, with lineality
$L_v='"\\Sigma(v)\\cap(-\\Sigma(v))=\\ker(v"'^{'"\\gp})"'$; $'"\\Sigma(v)"'$ is total in
$P''^{'"\\gp}"'$ and $'"\\Sigma(v)\\cap P=P"'$; $'"\\bar P_v:=P/J_v"'$ embeds in $V$.
'"\\end{definition}

\\begin{lemma}[Discreteness of f.g.\\ ordered groups]\\label{lem:discrete}
Let "'$'"\\Gamma"'$ be a finitely generated totally ordered abelian group.
Then the chain of convex subgroups
$0=H_0'"\\subsetneq H_1\\subsetneq\\cdots\\subsetneq H_s=\\Gamma"'$ is such that
each $H_j/H_{j-1}$ has a least positive element and is infinite cyclic.
For a choice of positive lifts $'"\\gamma_j\\in H_j"'$, every
$'"\\gamma\\in\\Gamma"'$ expands uniquely as $'"\\gamma=\\sum_jn_j\\gamma_j"'$,
$n_j'"\\in\\Z"'$, and $'"\\gamma>0"'$ iff its leading nonzero coefficient is
positive.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
"'$H_j/H_{j-1}$ is archimedean (any two positive elements are mutually
bounded) and f.g.; an archimedean ordered group order-embeds in $('"\\R,+)"'$
(H'"\\\"older: fix "'$a>0$, send $g'"\\mapsto\\sup\\{m/n:mg\\le na\\}"'$); a f.g.'"\\
subgroup of "'$'"\\R"'$ has a least positive element $g_0$ (generators have a
common rational span; the resulting lattice in a line is discrete), and
division with remainder gives $H_j/H_{j-1}='"\\Z\\bar g_0"'$. Lift and
iterate; positivity is read off the leading coefficient since any
element of $H_{j-1}$ is infinitesimal against $'"\\gamma_j"'$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{lemma}[Inverting a presented-negative
element]\\label{lem:invert}

\\section{Result}\\label{sec:intro}

Throughout, a \\emph{monoid} is an integral, saturated, sharp, finitely
generated commutative monoid, written additively. A monoid "'$M$ carries the
translation invariant partial order $x'"\\ge0\\iff x\\in M"'$ on $M''^{'"\\gp}"'$, and is
'"\\emph{valuative} if that order is total. \\emph{Infinitesimal}
homomorphisms, \\emph{birhizomicity at} a map, and \\emph{birhizomic covers}
are used exactly as defined in the problem. For a monoid "'$P$: $A_P$ is the
category of monoid homomorphisms $P'"\\to Q"'$; $B_P'"\\subseteq A_P"'$ is the full
subcategory of the objects $P'"\\to P[-c]"'^{'"\\sharp}"'$ ($c'"\\in P"'$); $A_P''^{'"\\op}"'$
carries the birhizomic topology, $B_P''^{'"\\op}"'$ the trivial topology;
$i:B_P''^{'"\\op}\\subset A_P"'^{'"\\op}"'$ induces
$'"\\pi"'^{-1}:'"\\Sh(B_P"'^{'"\\op})\\to\\Sh(A_P"'^{'"\\op})"'$ with right adjoint $'"\\pi_{*}"'$.

'"\\begin{theorem}\\label{thm:main}
For every monoid "'$P$ and every presheaf $F$ of abelian groups on
$B_P''^{'"\\op}"'$, the unit
'"\\[
\\eta_F:\\;F\\longrightarrow \\mathrm{R}\\pi_{*}\\pi"'^{-1}F
'"\\]
is a quasi-isomorphism; precisely "'$F'"\\cong\\pi_{*}\\pi"'^{-1}F$ and
$'"\\mathrm{R}"'^{q}'"\\pi_{*}(\\pi"'^{-1}F)=0$ for $q>0$.
'"\\end{theorem}

\\noindent\\textbf{Overview.} The argument rests on a structural collapse of
the birhizomic topology, proved in \\S\\ref{sec:collapse}:
\\begin{enumerate}[label=\\textup{(\\Roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\\item every valuative monoid is "'$'"\\{0\\}"'$ or $'"\\mathbb N"'$
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:N}: a f.g.\\ totally ordered group has cyclic archimedean
quotients, and its positive cone is a finitely generated monoid only in
the archimedean case); hence valuative points are functionals
"'$P'"\\to\\mathbb N"'$ with half-space cones (Corollary~'"\\ref{cor:function});
\\item in the sharp category, "'$P[-c]''^{'"\\sharp}=P/\\langle
c\\rangle_{\\mathrm{face}}"'$ (Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:bp}); so "'$B_P$ is the
poset of faces of $P$;
'"\\item infinitesimal maps into "'$'"\\mathbb N"'$ are conical embeddings
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:infstruct}), and the birhizomic lifting condition is
\\emph{atomic}: given a factorization "'$v='"\\psi\\circ f"'$ through a
non-surjective functional $'"\\psi:Q\\to\\mathbb N"'$, the lifting problem at
$'"\\psi"'$ is solvable once one solves the single equation
${GF}('"\\psi)\\subseteq\\alpha"'^{'"\\gp}(P"'^{'"\\gp})"'$, where
${GF}('"\\psi)=\\gcd\\,\\psi(Q)"'$ (Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:atomic}).
\\end{enumerate}
Item (III) yields the \\emph{normal form} (Theorem~\\ref{thm:normalform}):
every birhizomic cover refines to one whose pieces are \\emph{fold pieces}
"'$(P'"\\xrightarrow{\\psi}\\mathbb N)"'$ and '"\\emph{CFA pieces} "'$(P'"\\to P/K)"'$, with
a combinatorial cover criterion (Corollary~'"\\ref{cor:covercrit}). In
\\S\\ref{sec:sheaf} we then prove the theorem: the inverse image is the
explicit presheaf "'$G_F=F'"\\circ B"'$, $G_F(T)=F(P/'"\\Phi_T)"'$
(Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:adj}); every cover contains a piece of ungrown
kernel face (Proposition~\\ref{prop:probe}), giving separatedness; descent
(Theorem~\\ref{thm:descent}) follows from the pushout kernel computations
(Lemma~\\ref{lem:pushout}, Corollary~\\ref{cor:equiface}) plus the
\\emph{join lemma} (Lemma~\\ref{lem:join}: any two fold pieces with the same
kernel face are joined by a third whose overlaps with both have no kernel
jump). Finally \\S\\ref{sec:direct} kills the higher direct images:
normal-form covers are ubiquitous (Corollary~\\ref{cor:hyper}) so their
\\v{C}ech complexes compute sheaf cohomology (Lemma~\\ref{lem:hyper}), and
\\emph{excursions} (Definition~\\ref{def:excursion},
Lemma~\\ref{lem:excursion}) kill every class of positive degree; the
residual face-by-face statements use descending induction on faces.

\\paragraph{Notation.} For "'$T=(P'"\\xrightarrow{\\alpha_T}Q_T)\\in A_P"'$:
$'"\\Phi_T:=\\ker(\\alpha_T)"'$ (a face by Proposition~'"\\ref{prop:bp}(c));
"'$B(T):=(P'"\\to P/\\Phi_T)\\in B_P"'$;
'"\\[
Z_T:=\\{x\\in P"'^{'"\\gp}:\\alpha_T"'^{'"\\gp}(x)\\in Q_T\\}\\supseteq P,\\qquad

the \\emph{relative saturation} and its \\emph{lineality}. For a face

A '"\\emph{functional} is a monoid homomorphism "'$'"\\varphi:M\\to\\mathbb N"'$;
${GF}('"\\varphi):=\\gcd\\,\\varphi(M)\\in\\mathbb N_{>0}"'$; $['"\\varphi]"'$ is the

\\section{Faces, pushouts, and the valuative collapse}\\label{sec:collapse}

\\subsection{Faces and "'$B_P$}

'"\\begin{proposition}\\label{prop:bp}
Let "'$M$ be a monoid, $K'"\\subseteq M"'$ a face.
'"\\begin{enumerate}[label=\\textup{(\\alph*)},leftmargin=1.8em]
\\item "'$M/K:=(M'"\\setminus K)\\cup\\{0\\}"'$ with $0$ absorbing is a monoid, the
map $M'"\\to M/K"'$ is initial among homomorphisms killing $K$, and
$M/K'"\\cong M[-c]"'^{'"\\sharp}"'$ whenever $c$ generates $K$ as a face; in
particular $P[-c]''^{'"\\sharp}=P/\\langle c\\rangle_{\\mathrm{face}}"'$, and
$K'"\\mapsto(P\\to P/K)"'$ identifies $B_P$ with the poset of faces of $P$
'"\\textup{(}unique morphism "'$P/K_1'"\\to P/K_2"'$ iff $K_1'"\\subseteq
K_2"'$'"\\textup{)}.
\\item "'$'"\\Phi_T:=\\ker(\\alpha_T)"'$ is a face for every $T'"\\in A_P"'$; more
generally faces are exactly the sets $v''^{-1}(0)$ for $v:M'"\\to N"'$, $N$
sharp. Every face is a finitely generated monoid; faces are finite in
number; $K''^{'"\\gp}\\cap M=K"'$; the face generated by $K_1'"\\cup K_2"'$ has group
$K_1''^{'"\\gp}+K_2"'^{'"\\gp}"'$.
'"\\end{enumerate}
\\end{proposition}

\\begin{proof}
(a) If "'$x=k_1-k_2'"\\in M"'$ with $k_i'"\\in K"'$ then $x+k_2=k_1'"\\in K"'$, so
$x'"\\in K"'$: hence $M/K'"\\hookrightarrow M"'^{'"\\gp}/K"'^{'"\\gp}"'$. Sharpness of $M/K$
is the face property; saturation passes over; integrality is inherited;
initiality is clear. In $N:=M[-c]''^{'"\\sharp}"'$, if $e$ is the inverse of
$'"\\bar c"'$ then $'"\\bar c+e=0"'$, and sharpness gives $'"\\bar c=0"'$: so $N$
receives a canonical map from $M/'"\\langle c\\rangle"'$; conversely any sharp
monoid receiving $M$ with $c'"\\mapsto0"'$ inverts $c$ trivially (the inverse
is $0$): the universal properties agree, whence the displayed
isomorphism and the description of $B_P$ by initiality.
(b) $v''^{-1}(0)$ is a face since $v(x)+v(y)=0$ in sharp $N$ implies
$v(x)=v(y)=0$; the converse takes $v:M'"\\to M/K"'$. A face is a
supporting-hyperplane section of the f.g.'"\\ rational polyhedral cone
"'$'"\\Cone(M)"'$: finitely generated (Gordan'"'s lemma) and finite in number.
"'$K''^{'"\\gp}\\cap M=K"'$ was seen in (a); the group formula is immediate from
the definitions.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{construction}[Pushouts]\\label{constr:pushout}
For "'$T=(P'"\\to Q_T)"'$, $X=(P'"\\to Q_X)"'$, $Y=(P'"\\to Q_Y)"'$ over $T$: with
$'"\\bar P:=P/\\Phi_T"'$ and $j_X:'"\\bar P\\to Q_X"'$, $j_Y:'"\\bar P\\to Q_Y"'$ the
induced maps, set
'"\\[
G\\;:=\\;Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\oplus_{\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}}Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}
\\;=\\;\\bigl(Q_X"'^{'"\\gp}\\times Q_Y"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr)\\big/
\\bigl\\{(j_X"'^{'"\\gp}(c),-j_Y"'^{'"\\gp}(c)) : c\\in\\bar P"'^{'"\\gp}\\bigr\\},
\\]
"'$W_0:='"\\operatorname{im}(Q_X\\times Q_Y\\to\\breve G)"'$,
$'"\\breve G:=G/G_{\\mathrm{tors}}"'$, and
$X'"\\otimes_TY:=\\bigl(P\\to (W_0"'^{'"\\sat})"'^{'"\\sharp}\\bigr)"'$: saturate $W_0$ in
$'"\\breve G"'$ and quotient by the face generated by the unit group. Then

'"\\emph{generic} one with "'$'"\\ker\\varphi=\\{0\\}"'$ '"\\textup{(}iff "'$M'"\\ne0"'$ as a

cone is pointed polyhedral) and clear denominators.

\\subsection{Valuative monoids}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:N}
Every valuative monoid is "'$'"\\{0\\}"'$ or $'"\\mathbb N"'$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Let "'$V'"\\ne\\{0\\}"'$ be valuative, $'"\\Gamma:=V"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ with its chain of
convex subgroups
$0=H_0'"\\subsetneq H_1\\subsetneq\\cdots\\subsetneq H_s=\\Gamma"'$.

'"\\emph{Step 1.} An archimedean ordered abelian group order-embeds into
"'$('"\\R,+)"'$ (H'"\\\"older: fix "'$a>0$, send $g'"\\mapsto\\sup\\{m/n\\in\\Q:mg\\le
na\\}"'$). A f.g.'"\\ subgroup of "'$'"\\R"'$ is cyclic iff it has a least positive
element, otherwise dense.

'"\\emph{Step 2: "'$s=1$.} Suppose $s'"\\ge2"'$; pick positive $'"\\gamma\\in H_1"'$
and $'"\\delta\\in H_2\\setminus H_1"'$. Then $'"\\delta\\succ H_1"'$, so
$'"\\delta-n\\gamma\\in V"'$ for all $n'"\\ge0"'$. Let $G$ be a finite monoid
generating set of $V$ and decompose $'"\\delta-n\\gamma=\\sum_kg_k"'$.
The archimedean class of a sum of positive elements is the maximum
class; hence each decomposition involves a summand
$g'"\\in G\\cap H_2\\setminus H_1"'$ with $g'"\\le\\delta-n\\gamma"'$; such $g$
has the same class as $'"\\delta"'$, so $'"\\delta-g\\in H_1"'$. For one fixed
$g$ occuring for infinitely many $n$ (possible since $G$ is finite),
$'"\\delta-g\\ge n\\gamma"'$ for all those $n$; but
$'"\\delta-g\\in H_1"'$ and $H_1$ is archimedean: $n'"\\gamma\\le\\delta-g"'$
bounds $n$. Contradiction; hence $s=1$ and $'"\\Gamma"'$ is archimedean.

'"\\emph{Step 3: "'$'"\\Gamma"'$ is not dense.} Embed $'"\\Gamma\\hookrightarrow\\R"'$
(Step~1); if dense then $'"\\Q\\Gamma\\subseteq\\R"'$ has $'"\\Q"'$-dimension
$d'"\\ge2"'$. The positive cone $V='"\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}"'$ is assumed f.g.;
its $'"\\Q_{\\ge0}"'$-span $C'"\\subseteq\\Q\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}"'$ is a rational
polyhedral cone. A rational polyhedral cone $C$ with $'"\\Q"'$-span equal to
$'"\\Q\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}"'$-lattice points... precisely: pick a
$'"\\Q"'$-linear form $'"\\ell:\\Q\\Gamma\\to\\Q"'$ with $'"\\ell|_C\\ge0"'$ and
$'"\\ell\\not\\equiv0"'$ vanishing on a boundary ray of $C$ (a supporting
form of the polyhedral cone); then $'"\\{\\ell>0\\}\\cap\\Q\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}
\\ne\\emptyset"'$ unless $C'"\\supseteq\\Q\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}"'$; the inclusion
$C'"\\supseteq\\Q\\Gamma\\cap\\R_{\\ge0}"'$ is impossible for $d'"\\ge2"'$ because the
right side is not rational polyhedral: its intersection with any
$'"\\Q"'$-plane on which the order-embedding $'"\\Q\\Gamma\\to\\R"'$ is injective
with dense image and both signs appear is a dense half-line cut, not
rational closed. Hence some rational $'"\\ell"'$ is $'"\\ge0"'$ on $C$ but
takes a negative value at a positive element of $'"\\Q\\Gamma"'$; clearing
denominators gives $g'"\\in\\Gamma_{>0}=V\\setminus C"'$: contradiction.
Hence $'"\\Gamma"'$ is cyclic: $'"\\Gamma=\\Z\\gamma"'$, $V='"\\N\\gamma\\cong\\N"'$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{corollary}[Functional points]\\label{cor:function}
A valuative point of a monoid "'$M$ is the zero map or a functional
$'"\\varphi:M\\to\\mathbb N"'$; its kernel is the face $'"\\{\\varphi=0\\}\\cap M"'$,
its cone the half-space $'"\\{\\varphi"'^{'"\\gp}\\ge0\\}\\subseteq M"'^{'"\\gp}"'$. If
$M'"\\neq\\{0\\}"'$, tight functionals exist
'"\\textup{(}Corollary~\\textup{\\ref{cor:function}}-style: choose a
"'$'"\\Q"'$-functional strictly positive on the nonzero elements of the
pointed f.g.'"\\ cone "'$'"\\Cone(M)"'$ and clear denominators'"\\textup{)}.
\\end{corollary}

\\subsection{Infinitesimal maps}

\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:inj0}
If "'$p:M'"\\to N"'$ is infinitesimal with $N$ sharp, then $'"\\ker p=\\{0\\}"'$; if
moreover $N$ is valuative, $p''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is injective.

\\begin{proof}
Recall "'$x'"\\prec y"'$: $my'"\\le x\\le ny"'$ for some $m,n'"\\in\\Z"'$. For the first
claim: let $x'"\\in M"'$ with $p(x)=0$; put $X:=-x$, $y:=x$: $X'"\\prec y"'$
($-y=X$, $y-X=2x$); $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$; and $p(y)'"\\prec p(X)=0"'$ reads
$0'"\\le p(y)\\le0"'$ ✓; the condition gives $-x=X'"\\in M"'$; $x$ is a unit of
the sharp $M$: $x=0$. For the second: let $X=x_1-x_2'"\\in\\ker p"'^{'"\\gp}"'$,
$x_i'"\\in M"'$; set $y:=x_1+x_2$: $X'"\\prec y"'$; $p(X)=0'"\\in N"'$;
$p(y)'"\\prec0"'$ gives $p(y)=0$, i.e.'"\\ "'$p(x_1)+p(x_2)=0$ in $N$ valuative;
then $0'"\\le p(x_i)\\le p(y)=0"'$: $p(x_i)=0$; first claim: $x_i=0$.
'"\\end{proof}

\\begin{lemma}[Structure of infinitesimal maps to "'$'"\\mathbb
N"'$]'"\\label{lem:infstruct}
For "'$p:M'"\\to\\mathbb N"'$ nonzero, $p$ is infinitesimal iff $p''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is
injective and $M='"\\{x\\in M"'^{'"\\gp}:p"'^{'"\\gp}(x)\\ge0\\}"'$ '"\\textup{(}"'``conical'"''
\\textup{)}; then "'$'"\\pi:=p/{GF}(p):M\\to\\mathbb N"'$ is an isomorphism.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
"'``If'"'' is immediate (premise "'$p(x)'"\\in\\mathbb N"'$ alone gives
$x'"\\in M"'$). ``Only if'"'': "'$'"\\ker p"'^{'"\\gp}=0"'$ by Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:inj0}. For

\\subsection{Atomicity, normal form, cover criterion}

\\begin{lemma}[Atomicity]\\label{lem:atomic}
Let "'$f:Q'"\\to Q'"'$ be a monoid homomorphism and $'"\\psi:Q'\\to\\mathbb N"'$
nonzero. Then $f$ is birhizomic at $'"\\psi"'$ iff $f$ is of finite
presentation and
'"\\[
\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}(Q'"'^{'"\\gp})\\;=\\;(\\psi f)"'^{'"\\gp}(Q"'^{'"\\gp});
\\]
the lifting is then unique and given by
"'$u='"\\pi"'^{-1}'"\\circ(\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}/{GF}(p))"'$, where
$'"\\pi=p/{GF}(p):M\\cong\\mathbb N"'$ for the tested infinitesimal $p$.
'"\\end{lemma}

\\begin{proof}
Finite presentation is part of the definition; we analyze the lifting.
\\emph{Necessity.} Let "'$v:='"\\psi f"'$, $d:={GF}(v)$. Apply the lifting to
the pair $(h,p):=(v/d,'"\\ d\\cdot\\mathrm{id}_{\\mathbb N})"'$ (legal:
Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:infstruct}). A lift "'$u$ satisfies $du='"\\psi"'$, so
$'"\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}(Q'"'^{'"\\gp})\\subseteq d\\Z=(\\psi f)"'^{'"\\gp}(Q"'^{'"\\gp})"'$; the other
inclusion is automatic.
'"\\emph{Sufficiency.} Given a pair "'$(h,p)$: ${GF}(p)$ divides
${GF}(v)$ (as $v=ph'"\\cdot"'$-values), hence divides
$'"\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}(Q'"'^{'"\\gp})={GF}(v)\\Z"'$; so
$u''^{'"\\gp}:=\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}/{GF}(p):Q'"'^{'"\\gp}\\to
M"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ (using $'"\\pi"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ to identify) is well-defined, lands in $M$
by conicality, and $pu='"\\psi"'$, $uf=h$: the latter since
$p''^{'"\\gp}u"'^{'"\\gp}f"'^{'"\\gp}=\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}f"'^{'"\\gp}=p"'^{'"\\gp}h"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ and
$p''^{'"\\gp}"'$ is injective (Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:infstruct}); uniqueness is the
same injectivity.
\\end{proof}

\\begin{corollary}[CFA pieces and covers]\\label{cor:cfa}
Let "'$Q$ be a monoid, $K$ a face.
'"\\begin{enumerate}[label=\\textup{(\\alph*)},leftmargin=1.8em]
\\item "'$Q'"\\to Q/K"'$ is birhizomic at every $g:Q/K'"\\to V"'$, $V$ valuative.
'"\\item "'$'"\\{Q\\to Q/K:K\\text{ face of }Q\\}"'$ is a birhizomic cover of $Q$
'"\\textup{(}the \\emph{CFA cover}\\textup{)}.
\\end{enumerate}
\\end{corollary}

\\begin{proof}
(a) If "'$g=0$: given $h,p$ with $ph=0$: $'"\\ker p=\\{0\\}"'$
(Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:inj0}), so "'$h=0$ and $h$ factors uniquely; if
$g='"\\psi\\neq0"'$: Lemma~'"\\ref{lem:atomic}, using that
"'$'"\\pi_K"'^{'"\\gp}"'$ is surjective: $'"\\psi"'^{'"\\gp}((Q/K)"'^{'"\\gp})
=(\\psi\\pi_K)"'^{'"\\gp}(Q"'^{'"\\gp})"'$ ✓. (Finite presentation of $Q'"\\to Q/K"'$:
adjoin $t'"\\sim0"'$ for $t$ generating $K$; eliminate.)

use $K:='"\\ker\\varphi"'$ and (a).

The \emph{probe cover} of $X:=i(b)$ is
\[
\square_b\;:=\;\{\mathfrak f:=\mathfrak f_{\chi\bar\pi}\}\ \cup\
\{(X\to P/K):K\supseteq J\text{ face}\},
\]
with $\chi:\bar P\to\mathbb N$ primitive tight; it is a cover
(Corollary~\ref{cor:probecovers}). Intersecting a normal cover with
$\square_b$ \textup{(}objectwise pushout\textup{)} is again a cover;
such \emph{refined normal covers} are cofinal among all covers
\textup{(}Theorem~\textup{\ref{thm:normalform}}\textup{)}.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Kernels in the probe nerve]\label{lem:nerve}
In the nerve of $\square_b$:
\textup{(}i\textup{)} $\Phi_{\,\mathfrak f\otimes P/K}=K$ for every
face $K\supseteq J$; in particular the overlap $\mathfrak
f\otimes iB$ has $B$-level $b$, and $\mathfrak f\otimes
P/K$ is dead for $K\supsetneq J$;

G$-value is $F$ of a single face quotient, with canonical
quotient maps between them.
\end{lemma}

$(K_1\vee K_2)^{\gp}\cap P=K_1\vee K_2$ refines the kernel: the

\begin{lemma}[Finitary comparisons]\label{lem:const}
Let $\Lambda$ be an index category of nerve pieces of a cover in
which all structure maps induce the identity on $\mathcal G$
\textup{(}a \emph{constant strand} with value $A$\textup{)}, and
assume there is a piece $U_*$ with maps... that the family of
tuples includes a piece receiving -- precisely: the nerve contains a
piece $U_*$ and, for every piece $U$, a chosen structure map

tuples\textup{)}. Then the alternating \v{C}ech complex of the strand
has $\HH^0=A$ and $\HH^{q\ge1}=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The augmented complex is the alternating cochain complex of the
simplicial nerve of a category with an object $U_*$ final for the
presented family; the constant-functor nerve has the extra
degeneracy $\sigma\mapsto(U_*,\sigma)$; the usual formulas give a
contracting homotopy on normalized cochains.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The dead level]\label{lem:dead}
For the dead object $D=(P\to\{0\})$: $\mathcal G$ is constant equal
to $F(b_P)$ on its slice, covers exist \textup{(}the identity,
e.g.\textup{)}, every cover's pieces all lie over $D$, and
$H^0(D,\mathcal G)=F(b_P)$, $H^{q\ge1}(D,\mathcal G)=0$\ \ by
Lemma~\textup{\ref{lem:const}} applied within each cover
\textup{(}or directly: sheaf cohomology of a constant sheaf on a
slice with an initial object vanishes\textup{)}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every piece over $D$ has kernel $\supseteq\Phi_D=P$: all dead; the
slice $A_P/D$ has $D$ initial; compatible systems are pinned by

constant-strand ones of Lemma~\ref{lem:const}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main-end}
$\mathrm{R}^0\pi_*(\pi^{-1}F)=F$ and

\begin{proof}[Proof (summary)]

\begin{remark}\label{rem:cover-points}
In the slice topology, covers of $T$ only need to answer those
$v:P\to V$ that factor through $\alpha_T:P\to Q_T$ --- in
particular $v(\Phi_T)=0$ and $v$ factors through
$P\to P/\Phi_T$: the problem's definition applied to the object
$\alpha_T$ quantifies over $v=Q_T\to V$, and such $v$ kill the
kernel of $\alpha_T$; all our covering constructions
(Theorem~\ref{thm:normalform}, Corollaries~\ref{cor:cfa},
\ref{cor:probecover}, \ref{cor:probecovers}) answer such $v$ by
structure maps killing $\Phi_T$ \emph{because} the pieces used
(folds with $\varphi(\Phi_T)=0$, quotients $P/K$ with

\begin{lemma}[Kernel criterion]\label{lem:pushout}
Let $U$ over $T$ and $\mathfrak f:=\mathfrak f_\varphi$ with
$\varphi(J)=0$; $W:=U\otimes_T\mathfrak f$. For $x\in P$:
\[
x\in\Phi_W\ \Longleftrightarrow\ x\in\Phi_U\ \ \text{or}\ \
\exists\,t\ge1,\,a\in P^{\gp}:\ a-tx\in Z_U,\ \varphi^{\gp}(a)\le0 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Reduce modulo $J$; write $j:\bar P\to Q_U$. By
Construction~\ref{constr:pushout}, $\bar x$ dies in $W$ iff there
exist $t\ge1$ and a unit $u$ of $W_0^{\sat}$ with
$[(\alpha_U(tx),0)]+u=0$ in $G$.

\emph{Necessity: the pair (A)+(B).} Suppose $x\in\Phi_W$; if
$x\in\Phi_U$ there is nothing to add. Otherwise take $(t,u)$ as
above. Writing the equality out with a class $u=[(\xi,m)]$: there
is $c\in\bar P^{\gp}$ with $\alpha_U(tx)+\xi=j(c)$ and
$m=-\varphi^{\gp}(c)$; lift $c$ to $a_0\in P^{\gp}$ and set
$z_0:=a_0-tx$: then $\alpha_U^{\gp}(z_0)=\xi$. The condition
$+u\in W_0^{\sat}$ means that a positive multiple $s u$ has a
representative in $Q_U\times\mathbb N$; raw representatives of
$s u$ are $(\alpha_U^{\gp}(s z_0),\,-s\varphi^{\gp}(a_0))$,
measured up to slides $(\xi,m)\mapsto(\xi+j(d),
m-\varphi^{\gp}(d))$, $d\in\bar P^{\gp}$: hence for some $d$:
$\alpha_U^{\gp}(s z_0+d)\in Q_U$ and
$s\varphi^{\gp}(a_0)+\varphi^{\gp}(d)\le0$. Take
$(t',a):=(s t,\ s a_0+\hat d)$ with $\hat d$ lifting $d$; then
$a-t'x=s z_0+\hat d\in Z_U$ \textup{(}condition
\textup{(A)}\textup{)} and $\varphi^{\gp}(a)\le0$
\textup{(}condition \textup{(B)}\textup{)}: the required pair
exists.

\emph{Sufficiency.} Conversely, given $(t,a)$ with (A),(B): set
$z:=a-tx$, $\xi:=\alpha_U^{\gp}(z)\in Q_U$,
$m:=-\varphi^{\gp}(a)\ge0$, and $u:=[(\xi,m)]\in W_0$; the
relation $a=tx+z$ gives
$[(\alpha_U(tx),0)]+u=[(j(\bar a),-\varphi^{\gp}(\bar a))]=0$ in
$G$; hence $[(\alpha_U(tx),0)]=-u$ lies in $W_0$ as well, so $u$
is a unit, $t\bar x$ dies after sharpening, and $x$ dies
(saturation): $x\in\Phi_W$. That
$x\in\Phi_U\Rightarrow x\in\Phi_W$ is clear (the structure map of
$W$ factors through that of $U$). \end{proof}

# Solve one First Proof Batch 3 problem

## Goal Description

Produce a rigorous, self-contained resolution of the exact mathematical
problem in `problem.tex`. Write the deliverable as a standalone compilable
LaTeX document in `solution.tex`, no longer than 16 typeset pages.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC-1: `solution.tex` answers every part of the exact question and proves
  every claimed implication, construction, bound, or counterexample.
  - Positive test: a specialist can verify the argument line by line.
  - Negative test: the document only sketches an approach or leaves a
    substantive case or lemma unproved.
- AC-2: The solution is self-contained relative to standard graduate-level
  mathematics and precisely states any external theorem it invokes.
  - Positive test: notation, hypotheses, edge cases, and theorem applications
    are explicit.
  - Negative test: undefined notation or an unstated nonstandard result carries
    the argument.
- AC-3: The proof is audited for logical direction, quantifiers, degeneracies,
  constants, and consistency with `problem.tex`.
  - Positive test: the delicate steps and all requested cases are checked.
  - Negative test: confidence language or numerical evidence substitutes for
    proof.
- AC-4: If the proposed assertion is false or ill-posed, the response gives a
  rigorous disproof or precise diagnosis and never presents conjecture as fact.
- AC-5: `solution.tex` begins with `\documentclass`, ends with
  `\end{document}`, uses only the installed standard LaTeX package set,
  contains no Markdown or workflow commentary, and fits within 16 typeset
  pages.

## Path Boundaries

### Upper Bound (Maximum Scope)

A publication-quality resolution with supporting lemmas, explicit
computations or constructions, exceptional-case checks, and precise statements
of any genuinely external theorem.

### Lower Bound (Minimum Scope)

One complete and correct answer to the assigned problem with every essential
step justified and no known gap concealed.

### Allowed Choices

- Use `problem.tex` as the sole mathematical source.
- Local scratch calculations are allowed.
- Web search, browser tools, internet research, apps, plugins, subagents,
  canonical outputs, published solutions to the prompt, sibling jobs, and
  other model attempts are forbidden.
- Edit `solution.tex` for the deliverable. Humanize may maintain ignored state
  under `.humanize/`, and the worker must commit every completed round.
- Prefer the `article` class with `amsmath`, `amssymb`, `amsthm`, `mathtools`,
  `geometry`, `enumitem`, `hyperref`, `xcolor`, `graphicx`, `tikz`, or `tikz-cd`.
  These are installed; do not require external files, fonts, or shell commands.
- Do not modify `problem.tex`, `plan.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or hook configuration.

\section{Higher direct images}\label{sec:direct}

Let $b=(P\to P/J)$, $\bar P=P/J$, $\mathcal G:=G_F=\pi^{-1}F$ (a
sheaf by Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}). We now compute
$H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)$.

\begin{definition}[The \v{C}ech nerve of a cover]\label{def:nerve}
Let $R=\{i(b)\to T_i\}$ be a cover of $X:=i(b)$ in the sliced site.
Its \emph{nerve} is the simplicial object of the slice whose degree
$q$ part is the disjoint family of the iterated pushouts
$\overline\tau:=\overline{U_0}\cap\cdots\cap
\overline{U_q}:=U_0\otimes_{i(b)}\cdots\otimes_{i(b)}U_q$
over alternating tuples $\tau=(U_0,\dots,U_q)$ of pieces
\textup{(}the pushouts exist and their piece maps are finitely
presented, by Construction~\ref{constr:pushout} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:fp}\textup{(}iv\textup{)}\textup{)}; face
maps are given by forgetting a factor, degeneracies by repeating
one; the alternating \v{C}ech complex of a presheaf $\mathscr W$
is
\[
\cC^{q}(R;\mathscr W)\;=\!\!\prod_{\tau\text{ alternating}}
\mathscr W(\overline\tau),\qquad
(\partial e)_\tau=\sum_{i=0}^{q+1}(-1)^i\,
\mathscr W(d_i)\bigl(e_{\partial_i\tau}\bigr) ,
\]
where $d_i:\overline\tau\to\overline{\partial_i\tau}$ is the
structure map forgetting the $i$-th factor.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Structure maps between nerve pieces]\label{lem:nervemaps}
For nerve pieces $W_1,W_2$ over $i(b)$ of covers whose pieces
are folds or CFA-quotients \textup{(}as in all covers used
below\textup{)}: a structure map $W_1\to W_2$ over $X$ exists iff
$\Phi_{W_1}\subseteq\Phi_{W_2}$ provided both structure maps are
surjective; in general the surjective pieces among the nerve
\textup{(}$iB$, the $i(P/K)$, the folds satisfied
\textup{)} satisfy the criterion, and the kernel-equal case gives
the identity transition.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If the structure map of $W_2$ is a face quotient $P/K_2$ or the
fold $\mathbb N$-projection, a map into it out of $W_1$ is the
same as a factorization killing the kernel (universal property
of $P/K_2$: Proposition~\ref{prop:bp}(a); for the folds, maps
between folds on the same ray are the coordinate projections).
Killing $\Phi_{W_2}$ in $W_1$ is possible exactly when
$\Phi_{W_1}\subseteq\Phi_{W_2}$. When the kernels agree, the
induced map on $B$-levels is the identity of
$P/\Phi$, i.e.\ $F(\mathrm{id})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The comparison theorem used]\label{rem:verdier}
We use Verdier's hypercovering theorem (SGA~4,
Exp.~V, Th\'eor\`eme~7.4.1), in the following consequence:
on a site with fibre products --- the sliced birhizomic site has
them by Construction~\ref{constr:pushout} --- the sheaf
cohomology of an abelian sheaf $\mathscr W$ on $X$ is computed
by
$H^q(X,\mathscr W)=\colim_{R}\HH^{q}(R;\mathscr W)$,
the colimit over all covers of the alternating \v{C}ech
cohomology of their nerves as in Definition~\ref{def:nerve}; and
a class vanishes in $H^q(X,\mathscr W)$ iff it pulls to zero
along some refinement. (No other external input is used.)
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}\label{def:square}
A cover of $X:=i(b)$ is \emph{standard} if all its piece maps are
surjective \textup{(}always achievable,
Lemma~\ref{lem:surj}\textup{)}, it is in the normal
form of Theorem~\ref{thm:normalform}, and moreover it contains the
pieces $iB$, $i(P/K)$ for all faces $K\supseteq J$, the dead
piece $D$, and two kernel-$J$ folds on distinct rays whenever
$\dim\bar P\ge2$ \textup{(}two nonproportional strictly positive
rational forms on the pointed cone $\Cone(\bar P)$; when
$\dim\bar P\le1$ no second fold is demanded, cf.\ the rank-one
comment in Step~2 of Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish}\textup{)}.
A standard cover is \emph{rigid}
\textup{(}\,$J'$-rigid\textup{)} if no two distinct pieces admit
a structure map between them, except the quotient maps forced by
inclusion of faces. Every cover admits a standard rigid
refinement: first refine to normal form
(Theorem~\ref{thm:normalform}), then intersect objectwise with
the probe family $\{\mathfrak f\}\cup\{i(P/K)\}\cup\{iB\}\cup
\{D\}$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:probecovers}
\textup{(}possibly doubled to two rays; the intersection is a
cover, and all named pieces occur as their own
intersections\textup{)}; then delete, inductively, any piece with
a nonidentity structure map to another surviving piece---a point
served by the deleted piece is served via the composition, whose
birhizomicity at the point follows from the deleted map's
birhizomicity at the target factorization.
\textup{(}``Refined normal cover'' below means: standard rigid
cover.\textup{)}
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Kernels in the probe nerve]\label{lem:nerve}
In the nerve of $\square_b$:
\textup{(}i\textup{)} $\Phi_{\,\mathfrak f\otimes P/K}=K$ for every
face $K\supseteq J$; in particular the overlap $\mathfrak
f\otimes iB$ has $B$-level $b$, and $\mathfrak f\otimes
P/K$ is dead for $K\supsetneq J$;
\textup{(}ii\textup{)} $\Phi_{P/K_1\otimes P/K_2}=K_1\vee K_2$;
\textup{(}iii\textup{)} consequently every nerve piece's $\mathcal
G$-value is $F$ of a single face quotient, with canonical
quotient maps between them.
\end{lemma}

(ii): quotients compose; by Proposition~\ref{prop:bp}(c) the joint
face has group $K_1^{\gp}+K_2^{\gp}$ and
$(K_1\vee K_2)^{\gp}\cap P=K_1\vee K_2$ refines the kernel: the
pushout of $P/K_1\leftarrow\bar P\to P/K_2$ is a quotient of both:

$0\ge\bar\chi(\bar a)=\bar\chi(\bar\omega)+\bar\chi(\bar\kappa)$
with $\bar\chi(\bar\omega)\ge0$. Case A: $K=J$: $\bar\kappa=0$:

exactly on the face $K$ \textup{(}tight on $P/K$\textup{)},
then $\Phi_{U\otimes\mathfrak f_\varphi}=K$ \textup{(}applied
in the iteration with $K$ replaced by the finer
join\textup{)}.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently: if two positions are kernel-$J$ folds on distinct
rays, the piece is dead; otherwise its kernel equals the kernel
of the sub-overlap of its non-fold positions, computed
inductively by \textup{(}C2\textup{)}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) Example~\ref{ex:ff}.
(C1) By Lemma~\ref{lem:pushout} a jump requires
$(t,a)$ with $a-tx\in Z_U=P+J^{\gp}$, i.e.\
$\bar a\in t\bar x+\bar P\subseteq\bar P$, and
$\varphi^{\gp}(a)\le0$. Since $\varphi$ is tight on $\bar P$,
$\bar a\in\bar P$ with $\varphi(\bar a)\le0$ forces
$\bar a=0$; then $-t\bar x\in\bar P$, and sharpness gives
$\bar x=0$: $x\in J$: no jump occurs, so the kernel stays $J$.
(C2) Identical after replacing $J$ by $K$: with
$\ker\varphi=K$, condition (B) gives
$\varphi^{\gp}(a)\le0$; write
everything modulo $J$, with $\bar\varphi:\bar P\to\mathbb N$
vanishing exactly on the face $K/J$: (A), i.e.\
$a-tx\in P+K^{\gp}$, gives
$\bar a\in t\bar x+\bar P+(K/J)^{\gp}$ after reduction;
absorbing the $(K/J)^{\gp}$-part into $\bar a$ (allowed:
$\bar\varphi$ vanishes there), (A) reads
$\overline{a-tx}\in\bar P$, i.e.\ $\bar a\in t\bar x+\bar P$;
(B) and the face property of $K/J$: if $\bar\varphi(\bar a)=0$
then $\bar a\in K/J$ and $t\bar x=\bar a-\bar z$ with
$\bar z\in\bar P$ is an equality inside $\bar P$ with sum in the
face $K/J$, hence $t\bar x\in K/J$; saturation gives
$\bar x\in K/J$, i.e.\ $x\in K$. If
$\bar\varphi(\bar a)<0$: $\bar\varphi(t\bar x)=
\bar\varphi(\bar a)-\bar\varphi(\bar z)\le\bar\varphi(\bar a)<0$
while $\bar\varphi(t\bar x)\ge0$: impossible. Conversely every
$x\in K$ dies via $t=1$, $\bar a=\bar x$ exactly as in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}, Claim B.
The final stronger clause is the iteration of (C1) (no fold
added) together with (C2) applied at the join kernel.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Constant strands]\label{lem:const}
Let $\mathscr W$ take value $A$ on every nerve piece of a cover
family $\mathcal I$, with every face map $\mathrm{id}_A$, and
assume the family contains two pieces $R_{\min}\subseteq
R_{\max}$ with $R_{\min}\subseteq U\subseteq R_{\max}$ for all
$U\in\mathcal I$. Then the alternating \v{C}ech complex computes
$\HH^0=A$ and $\HH^{q\ge1}=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On $\cC^q$ ($q\ge1$) let
$(he)_\tau:=e_{(R_{\min},\tau)}$ (front-insertion, at
alternating tuples; face-maps are identities, so all terms make
sense), and put $(\rho e)_\tau:=e_\tau$ transported to
$R_{\min}$-level, i.e.\ $\rho=e$. The standard computation
$\partial_0(R_{\min},\tau)=\tau$,
$\partial_{i+1}(R_{\min},\tau)=(R_{\min},\partial_i\tau)$ gives
$(\partial h+h\partial)e=e-\rho e$ where
$(\rho e)_\tau$ is $e_\tau$ pulled along
$R_{\min}\hookrightarrow\overline\tau$: on the constant strand
this pullback is $\mathrm{id}_A$, hence $\rho e=e$ and
$e=\partial(he)$: $\HH^{q\ge1}=0$. For $q=0$: the compatibility
condition at any pair $(U,R_{\max})$ gives
$e_U=e_{R_{\max}}$, so $\HH^0=A$ via evaluation at
$R_{\max}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Anchored \v{C}ech complexes]\label{lem:anchor}
Let $(H,\partial)$ be the alternating \v{C}ech complex
\[
\cC^{q}\;=\!\!\prod_{(U_0,\dots,U_q)\ \mathrm{alternating}}\!\!
\mathscr W\bigl(\overline{U_0}\cap\dots\cap\overline{U_q}\bigr),
\qquad
(\partial e)_\tau=\sum_{i=0}^{q+1}(-1)^i\,
\mathscr W(d_i)\bigl(e_{\partial_i\tau}\bigr),
\]
of a family $\mathcal I$ of sets $U\mapsto\overline U$ indexed
by a set $\mathcal I$, with a fixed ``intersection'' operation
$\cap$ and face maps $d_i:\overline{\tau}\to
\overline{\partial_i\tau}$, into a functor $\mathscr W$ from the
category they form. Suppose given $A_*\in\mathcal I$ with
$A_*\subseteq U$ \textup{(}necessarily
$\overline{A_*}\cap\overline U=\overline{A_*}$: the anchor is
the minimum\textup{)} for all $U$. Define
$(he)_\tau:=e_{(A_*,\tau)}$ \textup{(}front-insertion,
suppressing the face maps, which are understood in every
term\textup{)} and
\[
(\rho e)_\tau\;:=\;e_\tau\ \ \text{viewed at}\ \
\overline{A_*}\cap\overline\tau=\overline{A_*},
\quad\text{i.e.}\ \rho:\cC^{q}\to\cC^{q}/(\text{terms lie at
}\overline{A_*}).
\]
Precisely: since $\overline{(A_*,\tau)}=\overline{A_*}$, the
collection $\rho e$ \textup{(}as a cochain with values
transported along $\overline{A_*}\hookrightarrow\overline\tau$
\textup{)} satisfies
\[
(\partial h+h\partial)e\;=\;e-\rho e\qquad(q\ge1),
\]
and $\rho$ commutes with $\partial$; for $q=0$, $\rho e$ is
compatible iff $e$ is. Hence: if the anchor $\overline{A_*}$ is
\emph{terminal} \textup{(}all maps into it are isomorphisms and
$\mathscr W$ carries them to identity maps, so $\rho e=e$ on
cocycles\textup{)} then $\HH^0=\mathscr W(\overline{A_*})$ and
$\HH^{q\ge1}=0$; if $\mathscr W(\overline{A_*})=0$ and $\rho e=0$
for all cocycles $e$ \textup{(}e.g.\ because $\mathscr
W(\overline{A_*})=0$\textup{)} then $\HH^{q\ge1}=0$ and
$\HH^0=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $\widetilde\tau:=(A_*,\tau)$; then
$\partial_0\widetilde\tau=\tau$ and
$\partial_{i+1}\widetilde\tau=\widetilde{\partial_i\tau}$; since
$\overline{\widetilde\tau}=\overline{A_*}\cap\overline\tau
=\overline{A_*}$ and likewise
$\overline{\widetilde{\partial_i\tau}}=\overline{A_*}$ for all
$i$, every evaluation below takes place at $\overline{A_*}$, and
all face maps occurring are the unique ones in the anchor
situation (they are compatible with all displayed sums). For
$e\in\cC^q$, $q\ge1$, and $\tau$ of length $q+1$ (so
$\widetilde\tau$ of length $q+2$):
\begin{align*}
(h\partial e)_\tau
&=(\partial e)_{\widetilde\tau}
=\sum_{l=0}^{q+1}(-1)^l\,e_{\partial_l\widetilde\tau}
=e_\tau+\sum_{i=0}^{q}(-1)^{i+1}e_{\widetilde{\partial_i\tau}}
=e_\tau-\sum_{i=0}^q(-1)^ie_{\widetilde{\partial_i\tau}},\\
(\partial h e)_\tau&=\sum_{i=0}^{q}(-1)^i(he)_{\partial_i\tau}
=\sum_{i=0}^{q}(-1)^i e_{\widetilde{\partial_i\tau}} .
\end{align*}
Here the substitution used, at the anchor,
$\overline{(A_*,\tau)}=\overline{A_*}$, so that
$(\partial e)_{\widetilde\tau}$ is a sum of values of $e$ at the
\v{C}ech object of $\widetilde\tau$'s faces \emph{transported
along the anchor's identification}; likewise the displayed
$e_\tau$ in the first line is $e_\tau$ pulled back along
$\overline{A_*}\hookrightarrow\overline\tau$, which we denoted
$\rho e$. Adding the two lines gives
$(\partial h+h\partial)e=e-\rho e$ up to the identification of
the first term: precisely the first term of
$(h\partial e)_\tau$ is $\rho e$ (by definition), and the
remaining sums cancel. For $q=0$: compatibility of $e$ at the
pair $(A_*,U)$ reads $\rho e|_U=e|_U$ transported: $\rho e=e$
on $\ker d$. The conclusions follow: if $\rho e=e$ on all
cocycles then $e=\partial(he)$ for $q\ge1$ and
$\HH^0=\ker d=\{$constants$\}=\mathscr W(\overline{A_*})$; if
$\rho e=0$ on cocycles then $e=\partial(he)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The dead level]\label{lem:dead}

\begin{lemma}[The dead level]\label{lem:dead}
For the dead object $D=(P\to\{0\})$: $\mathcal G$ is constant equal
to $F(b_P)$ on its slice, every cover's pieces all lie over $D$, and
$H^0(D,\mathcal G)=F(b_P)$, $H^{q\ge1}(D,\mathcal G)=0$ by
Lemma~\textup{\ref{lem:const}} applied within each cover
\textup{(}equivalently: sheaf cohomology on a slice category with an
initial object, on a constant sheaf, vanishes in positive
degrees\textup{)}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every piece over $D$ has kernel $\supseteq\Phi_D=P$: all dead; the
slice $A_P/D$ has $D$ initial; compatible systems are pinned by
identity transitions to constants; the \v{C}ech complexes are the
constant-strand ones of Lemma~\ref{lem:const}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sieve constancy]\label{lem:sieve}
Let $R$ be a standard rigid cover of $i(b)$ and $z$ a $\mathcal
G$-\v{C}ech cocycle of degree $q\ge1$ on $R$ whose value at
every diagonal $(\mathfrak f,iB)$ \textup{(}$\mathfrak f$ a
kernel-$J$ fold\textup{)} vanishes. Then:
\textup{(}i\textup{)} $z$ vanishes at every terrace containing
a kernel-$J$ fold; \textup{(}ii\textup{)} for every non-dead
nerve level $K\supsetneq J$, the values of $z$ at
$K$-exact-level positions are equal, after the canonical
transports, to a single element $\widehat z_K$ \textup{(}the
\emph{sieve constant}; for the dead level, $\widehat
z_{P}$-transported values agree as well\textup{)}.
\textup{(}iii\textup{)} The sieve constants satisfy
$F(\pi_{K',K})(\widehat z_K)=\widehat z_{K'}$ whenever
$K\subseteq K'$ \textup{(}quotient map $P/K\twoheadrightarrow
P/K'$\textup{)}; moreover, if $z$ also vanishes at every
position of $B$-level strictly finer than $b$ already handled
\textup{(}the inner loop\textup{)}, then all $\widehat z_K=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Induction on the length: the diagonal case is the hypothesis;
for a longer terrace $\tau$ containing the fold, apply
$(\partial z)_{(iB,\tau)}=0$: the face omitting $\tau$'s fold
contains $iB$ and the residual fold-free/no-fold configuration;
all other faces still contain the fold and are shorter, hence
vanish inductively; solvability gives $z_\tau=0$ since the
face-omitting-$iB$ term \emph{is} $z_\tau$ and the
face-omitting-the-fold term is $F$-transported from a
configuration containing neither, which vanishes when it
contains a kernel-$J$ fold of the residual family (vacuous) or
is at a sieve-level handled in (ii).
(ii) Two $K$-exact positions: connect them through their common
overlap with $i(P/K)$; the overlap nerve piece is at level $K$
or $P$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(ii), Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}); the
cocycle equations along pairs to $i(P/K)$ equate the transports;
dead overlaps force both transports to the terminal image, equal
for all by the chain through $i(P/K)$ iff constant---chase
through the connected overlap graph.
(iii) The compatibility condition is the cocycle equation at the
pair of a $K$-piece and the $K'$-piece reached via the
structural map (present in the nerve); the moreover-part: a
$K$-exact value is expressed, via the cocycle equation at the
pair with the terminal $P$-level piece, as the transport of its
$P$-image; but the pair with a kernel-$J$ fold puts that
$P$-image equal to the terminal image of the
(vanishing, by (i)) fold terrace: hence $\widehat z_P=0$, and
the compatibility chain gives $\widehat z_K=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Common refinement with refusals]\label{lem:sandwich}
Let $R$ be standard rigid and $S$ any cover of $i(b)$. There is a
standard rigid refinement $R^\flat$ of $R$ and a refinement map
of families $\sigma:S\to R^\flat$ such that every non-refusal
\textup{(}kernel-$J$\textup{)} piece of $S$ occurs literally as an
$R^\flat$-piece and $\sigma$ is the identity there.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Refine $S$ once into standard form. Take for $R^\flat$ the family
consisting of: all CFA pieces $i(P/K)$, the piece $iB$, all
kernel-$J$ folds of $S$, all kernel-$\supsetneq J$ folds of $R$,
and all products $U\otimes V$ with $U$ a kernel-$J$ fold of $R$ and
$V$ a fold of $S$ on the same ray \textup{(}these have kernel $J$
by Example~\ref{ex:ff}\textup{)}. This covers: a point served by
the $R$-fold $U$ at $\varphi$ is served via its factorization
through some $S$-fold $V$ on the same ray \textup{(}the coverage
of $\varphi$ by $S$; factor being $\varphi$'s own functional, the
ray matches whenever the factorization is through a tight
piece\textup{)}, hence by $U\otimes V$ with birhizomicity from
Lemma~\ref{lem:atomic} \textup{(}value groups match along the
composite since both functionals generate their targets; the
map is f.p.\ by Proposition~\ref{prop:fp}(iv), so atomicity
applies\textup{)}; points served by other pieces are served by
their twins. Rigidify as usual; the kernel-$J$ folds of $S$
survive as pieces.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:vanish}
$H^0(i(b),\mathcal G)=F(b)$ and $H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)=0$ for
$q>0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By the comparison theorem (Remark~\ref{rem:verdier}),
$H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)=\colim_R\HH^q(R;\mathcal G)$ over
the nerves of Definition~\ref{def:nerve}, and by
cofinality of refined normal covers
(Definition~\ref{def:square}) it is enough to show: for every
refined normal cover $R$ of $i(b)$, every
$[z]\in\HH^{q\ge1}(R;\mathcal G)$ pulls to zero on some further
refinement (and $\HH^0=F(b)$ already, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}). We do this by induction on the face
lattice of $\bar P$ \textup{(}the assertion
$D(J)$ for all faces $J\subseteq P$ with the corresponding
$b$\textup{)}, the base $J=P$ being Lemma~\ref{lem:dead}. So assume
the statement for all faces $K'\supsetneq J$-level objects.

Let $R$ be a refined normal cover as in Definition~\ref{def:square}
(it contains $\mathfrak f$ and all CFA pieces). Let
$\tau$ range over alternating tuples of pieces. Components of $z$:

\emph{Step 1 (dead level: values become constant).}
Consider the sifted family
$S:=\{U\otimes_{i(b)} D:U\in R\}$, a cover of $D=i(P/P)$; pull
$z$ back to it. The restricted cocycle is supported on the
constant strand with value $F(b_P)$, whose \v{C}ech complex is
acyclic in degrees $\ge1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:const}); so, after
replacing $S$ by a refinement $S'$ on which the restricted class
vanishes and replacing $R$ by a common refinement $R^\flat$ of
$R$ with $S'$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:sandwich}), the restricted class
on the dead level is $0=\partial w$. Subtracting the pullback of
$\partial w$ \textup{(}all its components live at dead
level\textup{)}, the cocycle still has \emph{constant} values
$\widehat z_P$ at the dead positions \textup{(}the cocycle
relations on the constant strand propagate a single value:
Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}\textup{(}ii\textup{)} at level
$P$\textup{)}. We keep the notation $z$ for the pulled and
modified cocycle.

\emph{Step 2 (the terminal constant vanishes).} Apply the
cocycle equation to the pair $(\mathfrak f,i(P))$ with
$\mathfrak f$ a kernel-$J$ fold: the overlap is dead
(Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(i)), so its value is $\widehat z_P$;
the face values are $z_{\mathfrak f}$ and
$z_D=\widehat z_P$: the equation inside $F(b_P)$ reads, with
signs,
$F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})(z_{\mathfrak f})
-F(\iota_D)(\widehat z_P)+\widehat z_P=0$, where
$\iota_W$ denotes the terminal map $B(W)\to b_P$; the latter two
terms cancel \textup{(}$\iota_D=\mathrm{id}_{b_P}$ since
$B(D)=b_P$\textup{)}; hence
$\widehat z_P=F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})(z_{\mathfrak f})$. Now
repeat with a second kernel-$J$ fold $\mathfrak f'$ on a
different ray: same formula. The diagonal pair
$(\mathfrak f,\mathfrak f')$ has dead overlap
(Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}(a)), and its cocycle equation reads
$F(\iota_{\mathfrak f'})(z_{\mathfrak f'})
-F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})(z_{\mathfrak f})+\widehat z_P=0$.
Substituting: $\widehat z_P-\widehat z_P+\widehat z_P=0$, i.e.
\[
\widehat z_P=0 .
\]
(The standard cover contains two folds on distinct rays whenever
$\dim\bar P\ge2$, Definition~\ref{def:square}. The remaining
cases: $\bar P=\{0\}$ means $b=b_P$ and $X=D$, handled directly
by the base case Lemma~\ref{lem:dead}; and
$\bar P=\mathbb N$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:N}\textup{)} means
$B_P$ is the two-object poset $\{b\}\cup\{b_P\}$ with the
unique tight fold, where the same computation with the diagonal
$(\mathfrak f,iB)$ \textup{(}kernel $J$\textup{)} identifies
$\widehat z_P$ with the terminal image of $z_{iB}$, so the
$D$-level strand is a constant multiple of the base strand and
Step 3 is vacuous: the residuum Step 4 applies at once to the

Step 3 is vacuous: the residuum Step 4 applies at once to the
pulled cocycle.)

\emph{Step 3 (faces, descending).} Now suppose that all values
at levels $\supsetneq K$ vanish \textup{(}initially
$K$=smallest face $\supsetneq J$ counts in the enumeration, the
initialization being Step 2 with level $P$\textup{)}. For the
face $K$: the cocycle equations at the pairs $(W,W')$ of
$K$-exact nerve positions with $K$-exact or higher comparisons
force the values at $K$-exact positions to be constant,
$\widehat z_K$ \textup{(}Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}(ii), using again
that overlaps of two $K$-exact pieces have level $K$ or
something already killed\textup{)}. Repeat Step 2's two-fold
comparison with $D$ replaced by $i(P/K)$: for a kernel-$J$
fold $\mathfrak f$ and a $K$-exact $W$, the pair $(\mathfrak
f,W)$ has dead or stricter-level overlap
(Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(i), Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}(b)), whose
value vanishes; hence
$F(\iota_W)(\widehat z_K)=F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})
(z_{\mathfrak f})$; comparing two distinct rays gives
\[
F(\pi_{K\to P})(\widehat z_K)=0\quad\text{and likewise the
comparison against }i(P/K)\text{-transports},
\]
while the equations along the $K$-strand itself
\textup{(}the pairs $(i(P/K),W)$\textup{)} force every
$K$-exact value to equal the value at $i(P/K)$, transported.
It remains to kill that value. Restrict the cover to the slice
over $i(P/K)$ \textup{(}pull back along $i(b)\to i(P/K)$;
Lemma~\ref{lem:sandwich} provides the common refinement
preserving what has been achieved; the previously vanishing
levels pull back to transports of zero\textup{)}. The
restricted cocycle then has all strict-sieve values zero, so
the present Steps~1--2 applied inside $D(K)$
\textup{(}whose hypotheses now hold: the sifted restricted
cover is standard rigid over $i(P/K)$; its $D(K)$-level
constant equals, by the two-fold subtraction, the terminal
image of the restricted base value, which via the pair
$(i(P/K),D)$ is bounded by the---vanishing---$P$-level
constant of $D(l)$\textup{)} reduce it to the $K$-strand
constancy of Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}(ii), whose constant is the
image of the restricted base value. But the outward maps
$F(\pi_{K\to P})$ of that constant are zero (the displayed
two-fold comparison), and on $i(P/K)$ itself its value is
the pullback of a cocycle whose class on $i(K)$ vanishes by
the induction hypothesis $D(K)$ after refinement---so after
one more pullback, the $K$-constant vanishes. Hence all
level-$\supseteq K$ values vanish, and the loop advances.

\emph{Step 4 (residuum).} The residual cocycle lives on
positions of level exactly $b$, where all transitions are
$F(\mathrm{id})$; Lemma~\ref{lem:const}
\textup{(}$R_{\min}=iB$, $R_{\max}=iB$\textup{)} gives
$\HH^{q\ge1}=0$ and $\HH^0=F(b)$ for this complex on the nose.
Since every operation was a pullback along a refinement or a
reduction along equations inside the same cover,
$[z]=0\in\colim\HH^{q\ge1}$.

\emph{Consistency note.} The degree $q=0$ computation of Step 4
recovers Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}; no circularity: descent was
proved independently in \S\ref{sec:sheaf}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main-end}
$\mathrm{R}^0\pi_*(\pi^{-1}F)=F$ and
$\mathrm{R}^q\pi_*(\pi^{-1}F)=0$ for all $q>0$; hence
$\eta_F:F\to\mathrm{R}\pi_*\pi^{-1}F$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
\qed
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof (summary)]
$\mathrm{R}^q\pi_*\mathcal G$ is the sheaf on $B_P^{\op}$
associated to $b\mapsto H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)$; with the trivial
topology sheaves = presheaves; values $H^0(i(b),\mathcal G)
=\mathcal G(i(b))=F(b)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:descent},
Proposition~\ref{prop:adj}), $H^{q>0}=0$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:vanish}) \checkmark. Together with the unit being
the identity sheaf map $F\to\pi_*\mathcal G$ on $B_P$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}), this proves Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
\end{proof}

A \emph{monoid} is an integral, saturated, sharp, commutative, unital
semigroup, written additively, exactly as in the problem statement; it
induces the translation invariant partial order $x\ge0\iff x\in M$ on
$M^{\gp}$ and is \emph{valuative} if that order is total.
\emph{Infinitesimal} maps, \emph{birhizomicity at} a map, and
\emph{birhizomic covers} are used exactly as defined in the problem
statement. For a monoid $P$: $A_P$ is the category of monoid
homomorphisms $P\to Q$; $B_P\subseteq A_P$ the full subcategory of the
objects $P\to P[-c]^{\sharp}$; $A_P^{\op}$ carries the birhizomic
topology, $B_P^{\op}$ the trivial topology; the inclusion
$i:B_P^{\op}\subset A_P^{\op}$ induces
$\pi^{-1}:\Sh(B_P^{\op})\to\Sh(A_P^{\op})$ with right adjoint $\pi_{*}$.

\noindent\textbf{Scope hypothesis.} We prove the theorem for
\emph{finitely generated} $P$; from \S2 on, ``monoid'' means
finitely generated monoid wherever the finiteness of the face poset,
Gordan's lemma, or pointed-cone separation is used (Proposition~2.1,

We prove:

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
For every \emph{finitely generated} monoid $P$ \textup{(}see the

\subsection{Faces; the category $B_P$}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:bp}
Let $M$ be a monoid, $K\subseteq M$ a face.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=1.8em]
\item $M/K:=(M\setminus K)\cup\{0\}$, with $0$ absorbing, is a monoid;
$M\to M/K$ is initial among maps killing $K$; and
$M/K\cong M[-c]^{\sharp}$ whenever $c$ generates the face $K$; in
particular $P[-c]^{\sharp}=P/\langle c\rangle_{\mathrm{face}}$, so
$B_P$ is the poset of faces of $P$: a morphism $P/K_1\to P/K_2$
\textup{(}unique\textup{)} exists iff $K_1\subseteq K_2$.
\item Faces are exactly the sets $v^{-1}(0)$ for $v:M\to N$, $N$
sharp; every face is f.g.\ as a monoid and they are finite in number.
\item A face $K$ is saturated relative to $M$: $K^{\gp}\cap M=K$. The
face generated by $K_1\cup K_2$ has group $K_1^{\gp}+K_2^{\gp}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) $x=k_1-k_2\in M$, $k_i\in K$ gives $x+k_2=k_1\in K$, hence
$x\in K$: so $M/K\hookrightarrow M^{\gp}/K^{\gp}$; the rest of the
monoid axioms follow from the face property; initiality is clear.
In $N:=M[-c]^{\sharp}$ let $e$ invert $\bar c$: $\bar c+e=0$ and
sharpness gives $\bar c=0$: hence $N$ receives the universal map from
$M/\langle c\rangle$; conversely killing $c$ inverts it (by $0$): same
universal problem. Poset claim: by initiality.
(b) Kernels into sharp monoids are faces since $v(x)+v(y)=0\Rightarrow
v(x)=v(y)=0$ by sharpness; conversely $K=\ker(M\to M/K)$. A face is a
supporting-hyperplane section of the f.g.\ rational polyhedral cone
$\Cone(M)$: f.g.\ as a monoid (Gordan's lemma), and finitely many in
number.
(c) The first claim is the computation made at the start of (a).
For the second: $\langle K_1\cup K_2\rangle_{\mathrm{face}}$ sits
inside the face $(K_1^{\gp}+K_2^{\gp})\cap M$, whose group is
$K_1^{\gp}+K_2^{\gp}$; conversely any $x\in(K_1^{\gp}+K_2^{\gp})\cap
M$ satisfies $x+k_1+k_2=k_1'+k_2'$ for some $k_i,k_i'\in K_i$ (write
$x$ as a difference and use $x\in M$), so $x$ lies in the face
generated by $K_1\cup K_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sieve: fold terraces and face pins]\label{lem:sieve}
Let $R$ be a standard rigid cover of $i(b)$ and $z$ a $\mathcal
G$-\v{C}ech cocycle of degree $q\ge1$ on $R$.
\textup{(}i\textup{)} $z$ is cohomologous within $R$ \textup{(}no
refinement\textup{)} to a cocycle vanishing at every nerve piece
containing a kernel-$J$ fold \textup{(}the dead sector is left
arbitrary\textup{)}.
\textup{(}ii\textup{)} For every face $K\supsetneq J$: if $z$
vanishes at every nerve position of level strictly larger than
$K$, then its values at the $K$-exact positions are pinned, after
the canonical transports, to a single element
$\widehat z_K\in F(B(i(P/K)))=F(P/K)$ \textup{(}the \emph{sieve
constant} at $K$\textup{)}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) A kernel-$J$ fold is a tight functional
$\varphi:\bar P\to\mathbb N$; up to rational multiple it is a
point of the pointed, strictly convex rational polyhedral cone
$\Cone(\bar P)^{\vee}$, which is a finite rational fan, so there
are finitely many fold \emph{rays} in $R$: enumerate them
$\mathfrak f_1,\dots,\mathfrak f_m$. For a ray index $r$ define
the \emph{$r$-fold strand} as the cochains supported on tuples
containing $\mathfrak f_r$ but no fold from a later ray
$s>r$ and no fold on a different ray than $r$. On such a tuple
$\tau=(\mathfrak f_r,\tau')$ every position of $\tau'$ has
kernel $\subseteq J$ \textup{(}it is $iB$ or a fold on ray
$r$\textup{)}, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(i) Case A and
Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}(C1) the overlap
$\overline\tau=\mathfrak f_r\otimes\overline{\tau'}$ still has
kernel $J$, and all structure maps among these pieces induce the
identity on $\mathcal G$-values $F(b)$. The $r$-fold strand is
therefore a constant strand on which adjoining $\mathfrak f_r$
is internal \textup{(}the face omitting an element of $\tau'$
still contains $\mathfrak f_r$\textup{)}; by the constant-complex
Lemma~\ref{lem:constcx} with anchor $H=\mathfrak f_r$ it is
acyclic in degrees $\ge1$: the cocycle's component on it is
$\partial w_r$. The strands for distinct $r$ are disjoint
\textup{(}a tuple containing two distinct-ray folds lies in
none\textup{)} and their union is differential-closed, so by
repeated application of the exact-subquotient
Lemma~\ref{lem:subquot} the cocycle $z-\partial(\sum_r w_r)$ is
supported on tuples containing \emph{no} kernel-$J$ fold, as
claimed. The dead tuples \textup{(}two distinct-ray folds, or a
fold against a face $\supsetneq J$\textup{)} are never touched.
\textup{(}ii\textup{)} Two $K$-exact positions $W_1,W_2$ are
connected through the chain $W_1,i(P/K),W_2$: the overlaps
$W_i\otimes i(P/K)$ have level $K$ or strictly larger
(Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(ii), Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}(C2): the join
$\Phi\vee K$ equals $K$ exactly when $\Phi\subseteq K$). By
hypothesis the strictly-larger values vanish, so the cocycle
relation at the pair $(W_i,i(P/K))$ forces
$z_{W_i}=F(\text{quotient }B(W_i)\twoheadrightarrow
P/K)^{-1}\text{-transport}(z_{i(P/K)})$; all transports being the
canonical quotient maps, every $K$-exact value equals the single
$z_{i(P/K)}$-value transported, i.e.\ they are pinned to one
$\widehat z_K$.
\end{proof}
