\begin{proposition}\label{prop:vanish}
$H^0(i(b),\mathcal G)=F(b)$ and $H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)=0$ for
$q>0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By the comparison theorem (Remark~\ref{rem:verdier}),
$H^q(i(b),\mathcal G)=\colim_R\HH^q(R;\mathcal G)$ over the nerves
of Definition~\ref{def:nerve}, the colimit taken over the standard
rigid covers (cofinal by Definition~\ref{def:square}), which form a
directed system by the common-refinement
Lemma~\ref{lem:sandwich}. We prove
$\HH^0(i(b),\mathcal G)=F(b)$---true already on the nose:
$\mathcal G$ is a sheaf (Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}) and
$\mathcal G(i(b))=F(b)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:adj})---and that
every class $[z]\in\HH^{q\ge1}(R;\mathcal G)$ pulls to zero on a
further refinement. We work one degree $q\ge1$ at a time,
associating to a $q$-cocycle its $(q-1)$-\emph{faces} (the values
$z_{(U_0,U_1)}$), and use the sheaf axiom at each step to descend.
For $\bar P=\{0\}$ the slice is the dead level and
Lemma~\ref{lem:dead} gives the vanishing; for $\dim\bar P\le1$ the
whole nerve of a standard rigid cover is the constant strand with
minimum $iB$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:const}
($R_{\min}=R_{\max}=iB$) gives $\HH^{q\ge1}=0$ directly (these are
the base cases). Assume now $\dim\bar P\ge2$.

\emph{Step 1 (dead-sector hygiene).} Let $R$ be a standard rigid
cover. The sifted family $S:=\{U\otimes_{i(b)}D:U\in R\}$ is the
pullback of $R$ along $D\to i(b)$, hence a cover of $D$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:sandwich}); pass to the common refinement of $R$
and $S$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:sandwich} again) and keep the notation
$R$, $z$. Every nerve piece of $S$ is dead, and on the slice over
$D$ the sheaf $\mathcal G$ is the constant sheaf $F(b_P)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dead}); by the constant-complex
Lemma~\ref{lem:constcx} with anchor $H=D$, the restricted cocycle
is a coboundary: $z|_S=\partial w$ for a $(q-1)$-cochain $w$ on
$S$. Pulling $w$ back to $R$ along the refinement map, we may
subtract $\partial w$ from $z$; hence after this refinement
\[
\text{the value of }z\text{ at every nerve piece that maps to }D
\text{ is the value of a coboundary with coefficients in }F(b_P).
\tag{$\ast$}
\]
We assert nothing further about the dead sector; we do not pin it
to a single constant.

\emph{Step 2 (the terminal images of the folds agree).}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}(i) to $z$: it is cohomologous within
$R$ to a cocycle vanishing at every nerve piece containing a
kernel-$J$ fold; replace $z$ by this representative. In particular
$z_{\mathfrak f}=0$ for every kernel-$J$ fold $\mathfrak f$. For
two kernel-$J$ folds $\mathfrak f,\mathfrak f'$ on distinct rays
(available since $\dim\bar P\ge2$) the pairs
$(\mathfrak f,\mathfrak f')$, $(\mathfrak f,D)$,
$(\mathfrak f',D)$ are dead (Lemma~\ref{lem:mixed}(a),
Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(i)). Their cocycle values at degree
$q-1$ are, by $(\ast)$, coboundary values in $F(b_P)$:
$z_{(\mathfrak f,D)}=(\partial w)_{(\mathfrak f,D)}$ etc. The
values of a $q$-cocycle at the dead $(q-1)$-faces, being
coboundaries, impose no constraint beyond Step~1; the content we
retain is the equality of terminal images, already forced at the
sheaf level in Theorem~\ref{thm:descent}:
$F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})(z_{\mathfrak f})
=F(\iota_{\mathfrak f'})(z_{\mathfrak f'})=0$ in $F(b_P)$
since $z_{\mathfrak f}=z_{\mathfrak f'}=0$. (Here $\iota_W$ is the
terminal map $B(W)\to b_P$; the identification
$\bar\chi^{\gp}((K/J)^{\gp})=d\Z$, $d\ge1$, used in the kernel
computations is Lemma~\ref{lem:dlemma}.)

\emph{Step 3 (descending induction on faces).} We prove by
descending induction on the face $K\supseteq J$ that, after
refinement, $z$ is cohomologous to a cocycle vanishing at every
nerve position of level $\supsetneq K$; the base $K=P$ (dead
level) is Step~1's $(\ast)$ together with Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}(i)
(all fold terraces already vanish). For the inductive step suppose
$z$ vanishes at all levels strictly larger than $K$, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sieve}(ii) the $K$-exact values are pinned to a
single $\widehat z_K\in F(P/K)$. \emph{First, its image dies:} the
pair $(\mathfrak f,i(P/K))$ for a kernel-$J$ fold $\mathfrak f$ is
dead (Lemma~\ref{lem:nerve}(i)), so its value is a coboundary
value by Step~1's $(\ast)$, and the cocycle relation at that pair
reads $F(\iota_{i(P/K)})(\widehat z_K)
=F(\iota_{\mathfrak f})(z_{\mathfrak f})$ in $F(b_P)$; as
$z_{\mathfrak f}=0$ (Step~2) the right side is $0$, and
$\iota_{i(P/K)}=\pi_{K\to P}$, hence
\[
F(\pi_{K\to P})(\widehat z_K)=0\qquad\text{in }F(b_P).
\tag{$\dagger$}
\]
\emph{Then the constant itself dies:} restrict the cover to the
slice over $i(P/K)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:restrict}). The restricted
cocycle $z_K$ has, by Lemma~\ref{lem:restrict}(iii), its
$K$-exact constant equal to $\widehat z_K$; on the slice, the
piece $i(P/K)$ and its overlap with $iB$ have kernel exactly
$K$, and a $K$-exact face piece on the slice is precisely
$\overline{(W,iB)}$ for $W$ $K$-exact in $R$. The induction
hypothesis $D(K)$---vanishing of the same cohomology in the
degree one \emph{lower}, applied to the sheaf $\mathcal G_K$ on
the initial-object slice (Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} with
$T=i(P/K)$)---kills the face-values of $z_K$ at the
strictly-above-$K$ positions after one more refinement
(Remark~\ref{rem:transfer}); what remains on the slice is the
single class $\widehat z_K$ carried by $i(P/K)$. But
$(\dagger)$ says its only outward transition
$F(\pi_{K\to P})$ is zero, so $\widehat z_K$ is a class on the
constant-one-object strand that is annihilated; pulling back once
more (Remark~\ref{rem:transfer}) gives $\widehat z_K=0$. Thus $z$
vanishes at all $K$-exact positions, and the induction descends.

\emph{Step 4 (residuum and descent).} After the induction reaches
$K=J$ the cocycle vanishes at every nerve position of level
$\supsetneq J$, i.e.\ at every position containing a piece whose
kernel strictly contains $J$; the remaining positions have every
kernel equal to $J$, on which $\mathcal G$ is the constant sheaf
$F(b)$ with all transitions $F(\mathrm{id})$. On this residuum the
$\check H^{q\ge1}$ vanish and $\check H^0=F(b)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:const} ($R_{\min}=iB$, $R_{\max}=iB$). Since every
operation was a pullback along a refinement
(Remark~\ref{rem:transfer}) or subtraction of a coboundary within
one cover, $[z]=0\in\colim_R\HH^{q\ge1}(R;\mathcal G)$, and the
degree-$0$ assertion $\HH^0(i(b),\mathcal G)=F(b)$ is
Theorem~\ref{thm:descent} and Proposition~\ref{prop:adj}
\textup{(}no circularity: descent was proved independently in
\S\ref{sec:sheaf}\textup{)}. This completes the induction on $q$.
\end{proof}
